body: Luka Dončić is on one of the best scoring runs of his career. He had 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds in a 138-117 win over the Miami Heat on Nov. 2, and it was his fifth straight game with at least 37 points.
Four of those five games were 40-point nights, and he is averaging 43.4 points across the stretch. The game before Miami, he had 45 points and 15 assists in a win over Toronto.
## Why fans are buying in

Dončić is the defending NBA scoring champion, and he has picked up right where he left off. He has been especially sharp early in games, averaging 15 first-quarter points this season. Against Miami he had 16 in the first quarter alone and made six 3-pointers on the night.
The Lakers are winning with him. They are 6-2, and Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler gave him strong help against Miami, with Reaves scoring 27 and Kessler posting 15 points and 15 rebounds.

He was already one of the most popular players in the league. Dončić ranked No. 2 on the NBA's list of top-selling jerseys for the 2025-26 regular season, based on online sales through the NBA Store and the Fanatics network. In our analysis, a scoring run like this one keeps him at the center of the conversation and gives Lakers fans a fresh reason to wear his name. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look

Dončić wears No. 77, the number he has carried throughout his NBA career. His Lakers jersey comes in three styles, all shown in the banner above: the gold Icon Edition, the white Association Edition and the purple Statement Edition. Gold is the classic Lakers look, while the purple Statement version is the bolder choice.
## Why this jersey will last
Dončić is 27 and already established as one of the faces of the league, and the Lakers look like a contender early. The streak gets its next test on Wednesday in Sacramento.

body: Alperen Şengün ran the show as the Houston Rockets beat the Boston Celtics 109-93 on Nov. 2. The 24-year-old center scored 26 points on 12-of-15 shooting and added 10 assists, seven rebounds, two steals and two blocks.
Houston is now 7-1, and the win ended Boston's five-game winning streak.
## Why fans are buying in

Şengün is not a typical big man. He scores in the post, but he also runs the offense from the middle of the floor, and against Boston he set up teammates all night, including the Amen Thompson dunk that put the game away late. Houston outscored Boston 50-34 in the paint.

He has been building toward this for years. Oklahoma City drafted him 16th overall in 2021 and sent his rights to Houston on draft night. He became an All-Star in 2025 and made it again in 2026, making him the first player from Turkey to be a two-time All-Star. He also led Turkey to a silver medal at EuroBasket 2025, which gives him a following well beyond Houston.

The roster around him has young talent and veteran help. Jabari Smith Jr. had a double-double against Boston, Amen Thompson added 14 points and Kevin Durant chipped in 12. In our analysis, a big man who passes like a guard on a team that is winning early is exactly the kind of player whose jersey catches on. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
Şengün wears No. 28. His jersey shown in the banner above is the black Statement Edition, a sharp, modern look that stands apart from the classic red Rockets jersey.
## Why this jersey will last
Houston signed Şengün to a five-year extension in October 2024, so he is part of the team's plans for years to come. If the Rockets keep winning at this pace, he will be one of the main reasons.

title: Jason Robertson Jersey: Stars Winger's Natural Hat Trick
subheadline: Robertson scored three straight goals in 5:20 of the second period, the third-fastest hat trick in Stars history, in a 6-5 win in Washington.
description: Jason Robertson scored a natural hat trick in 5:20 in a 6-5 win over Washington on Nov. 3, third-fastest in Stars history. Why his No. 21 jersey is hot.
searchIntent: Stars and hockey fans who saw the hat trick want to know how fast it was and which Robertson jersey to get.
body: Jason Robertson needed just 5 minutes and 20 seconds to take over the Dallas Stars' game in Washington on Nov. 3. He scored three straight goals early in the second period, a natural hat trick, and added an assist as Dallas held on to beat the Capitals 6-5.
It was the third-fastest hat trick in Stars franchise history, behind only Tom McCarthy in 1984 and Jamie Benn in 2018.
## Why fans are buying in

The goals came in a hurry: a power-play goal 23 seconds into the period, another at 3:18 and a shot from the point at 5:43 that chased Washington's starting goalie. It was the seventh hat trick of Robertson's career and his third natural hat trick.
He has been one of the Stars' most productive players all fall, with eight goals and 18 points through 15 games. Dallas is 9-5-1 and has earned points in five straight road games.

Robertson's story has always had underdog appeal. Dallas took him in the second round in 2017, 39th overall, and he turned into a Calder Trophy finalist and then a 100-point scorer in 2022-23. Now 27, he plays on a deep team; on the same night, Mikko Rantanen reached 800 career points and Roope Hintz had three points. In our view, a homegrown scorer who keeps delivering big nights is the kind of player Stars fans build their collection around. This is our analysis, not a sales figure.
## The look

Robertson wears No. 21. His jersey comes in the Stars' kelly green home look, shown in the banner above. The bright green is one of the most recognizable colors in the NHL and an easy pick for game nights at American Airlines Center.
## Why this jersey will last
A second-round pick who became one of the league's top scorers is a player fans tend to stick with. With Robertson scoring at this pace, the Stars have a chance to climb in the Central.
